independent_execution.note: A 161496-byte measurement artifact containing all 1000 per-slot records across five levels regenerates byte for byte. Every figure in the manifest evidence line is real.

hidden_cases.rationale: The deliverable asks for a sweep across levels but the accept rule uses only two of them. I wanted the whole curve before judging the two-point comparison.
hidden_cases.construction: Ran the producer's run() on its own preregister and printed every level with its injected probabilities, throughput, escape fraction, production, review count and terminal backlog.
hidden_cases.interpretation: The sweep is real and the five levels are all genuinely computed, which satisfies the deliverable literally. Two structural facts emerge. The reviewed column is pinned at 800 for every level from 4 upward, because acceptance capacity is 4 per slot over 200 slots - so the primary metric, accepted good per slot, is bounded above by 4 by construction and has almost no room to move once concurrency exceeds capacity. And the curve is not monotone: throughput rises from 2.000 at concurrency 2 to 3.860 at concurrency 4, because at concurrency 2 the system is capacity-starved rather than contended. The accept rule therefore compares the peak of the curve against its worst point.

hidden_cases.rationale: The decisive question for any simulation: is the conclusion measured or assumed? defect_probability rises with concurrency-above-capacity by a hardcoded formula. If that formula is doing the work, the reproduction is a restatement of its own parameterisation. So I removed the formula and left everything else - the queues, the recovery loop, the seeding - untouched.
hidden_cases.construction: Replaced defect_probability with a constant 0.04 and re-ran the producer's run() on its own preregister.
hidden_cases.observed_output_verbatim:
conc | good/slot | escaped_frac
      2 |     2.000 |       0.0000
      4 |     3.860 |       0.0000
      8 |     3.840 |       0.0052
     16 |     3.820 |       0.0167
     32 |     3.825 |       0.0267
   verdict=PASS  refutation_triggered=False
   delta_throughput=-0.0350
hidden_cases.interpretation: The headline throughput effect collapses from -2.710 to -0.035, so 98.7 per cent of the reported effect is produced by the hardcoded defect formula rather than by unbalanced capacity. The residual -0.035 is a 0.9 per cent difference between 3.860 and 3.825 and is indistinguishable from sampling noise. And yet the verdict is still PASS, because the accept rule is a pure sign test with no magnitude floor. That is the finding: the preregistered acceptance rule returns PASS after I removed the mechanism it exists to detect.

hidden_cases.rationale: Follow the previous case to its end by removing the second injected formula as well, leaving pure queueing with no contention pressure of any kind.
hidden_cases.construction: defect_probability constant at 0.04 and detection_probability constant at 0.98, then re-ran run().
hidden_cases.interpretation: With no contention pressure modelled at all the accept rule still returns PASS, on a throughput delta of -0.035 and an escape delta of 0.0013. An acceptance criterion that fires at 0.0013 is not distinguishing anything. Contrast the sibling unit 050 in this same cohort, which preregistered a magnitude threshold of 0.20 - the right instinct, missing here.

hidden_cases.rationale: Rather than only attacking, I looked for whether the non-assumed result the hypothesis actually needs is available inside the producer's own model. It is, and it is stronger than what was reported.
hidden_cases.construction: With both pressure formulas held constant, so that nothing about defects depends on concurrency, computed accepted good results per ATTEMPT rather than per slot, alongside the terminal acceptance backlog.
hidden_cases.interpretation: This is the real result and the producer already had it. With zero injected pressure, independently accepted good output per attempt falls monotonically from 1.000 to 0.120 while the acceptance backlog grows to 5634 unreviewed attempts - driven purely by the fixed acceptance capacity, exactly the mechanism the frozen hypothesis names. The unit's chosen per-slot metric could not show this because it is capped at the acceptance capacity, which is why the injected defect formula had to carry the effect. The fix is a metric change, not a redesign, and I am recording the numbers so the re-run has a target.

hidden_cases.rationale: The verdict does by_level['4'] and by_level['32'] on a dictionary keyed from whatever levels the preregister lists. That couples the analysis to two specific magic values.
hidden_cases.construction: Ran run() with concurrency_levels of [2, 8, 16, 64], then [4, 32], then [1, 2, 3].
hidden_cases.observed_output_verbatim:
levels=[2, 8, 16, 64] -> KeyError: '4'
   levels=[4, 32] -> verdict=PASS
   levels=[1, 2, 3] -> KeyError: '4'
hidden_cases.interpretation: Any preregister that does not contain both 4 and 32 crashes with a bare KeyError. The sweep is therefore partly nominal: five levels are simulated and honestly reported per level, which is what the deliverable asks, but only two participate in the conclusion and those two are hardcoded rather than read from the preregister.

hidden_cases.rationale: Seed robustness, to separate a stable finding from a lucky seed.
hidden_cases.construction: Twenty independent seeds at 50 slots per level, recording both headline deltas and the verdict.
hidden_cases.observed_output_verbatim:
20 seeds: throughput delta -2.840 .. -2.440
   20 seeds: escape delta     0.531 .. 0.658
   verdicts: ['PASS'] (PASS count 20/20)
hidden_cases.interpretation: Entirely stable - 20 of 20 PASS with tight ranges. Taken with HC-C this stability is a property of the injected formulas rather than evidence of a robust empirical finding, but it does establish that the reported numbers are not a seed artifact and that the simulation is well behaved.

hidden_cases.rationale: The recovery loop mutates a defective item to non-defective and pushes it back into the acceptance queue, which is exactly the shape of code that double-counts. Internal accounting has to be checked before any of the headline numbers can be trusted.
hidden_cases.construction: For every level, checked that accepted_good + escaped_defects + detected_defects equals reviewed, and cross-checked recovered against detected and the terminal recovery backlog.
hidden_cases.observed_output_verbatim:
conc   2: accepted_good+escaped+detected=416 reviewed=416 match=True | recovered=16 detected=16 recovery_backlog=0
   conc   4: accepted_good+escaped+detected=800 reviewed=800 match=True | recovered=28 detected=28 recovery_backlog=0
   conc   8: accepted_good+escaped+detected=800 reviewed=800 match=True | recovered=94 detected=94 recovery_backlog=0
   conc  16: accepted_good+escaped+detected=800 reviewed=800 match=True | recovered=200 detected=200 recovery_backlog=0
   conc  32: accepted_good+escaped+detected=800 reviewed=800 match=True | recovered=248 detected=249 recovery_backlog=1
hidden_cases.interpretation: The accounting is exact at every level. Every reviewed item lands in exactly one of accepted, escaped or detected, and recovered plus the terminal recovery backlog reconciles against detected at every level including the off-by-one at concurrency 32, which is a single item still in the recovery queue when the run ends rather than a leak. This is careful work and I could not find a counting error.

producer_declared_limitations: Synthetic queue contention and review-sensitivity formulas do not estimate production provider latency or cost.
execution.json adds: The queue simulation freezes synthetic contention and review-sensitivity formulas; it does not estimate production provider latency or cost.
scope_honesty_assessment.assessment: The disclosure is genuinely good on the point that matters most. Saying the contention and review-sensitivity formulas are 'frozen synthetic' tells a reader that these are assumptions rather than observations, and the preregister goes further by publishing both formulas verbatim as defect_probability_formula and review_detection_formula. That is more transparency than most units in this wave offer, and it is what made HC-C possible for me to construct in two lines. What is not disclosed is the magnitude of the dependence - that the formula accounts for 98.7 per cent of the reported effect, and that the preregistered accept rule still returns PASS when the formula is removed entirely. Also undisclosed: that the primary metric is bounded above by the acceptance capacity, and that only two of the five swept levels enter the verdict.

reproducibility_check: Excellent. The 161496-byte measurement.json regenerates byte for byte with identical SHA-256 in a fresh isolated interpreter, and the headline deltas are stable across 20 independent seeds at -2.840 to -2.440 and 0.531 to 0.658.
vacuous_test_qualifier: Total for both tests. Neither exercises the queue simulation: one asserts the injected formulas are monotone, the other asserts the sign of two values returned by run(). A stub with no simulation at all passes both.
divergence_reason: The preregistered acceptance rule does not discriminate the finding it exists to detect, and I demonstrated that with the producer's own harness. Holding defect_probability constant while leaving the queues, the recovery loop and the seeding untouched collapses the headline throughput effect from -2.710 to -0.035, so 98.7 per cent of the reported effect is produced by a hardcoded formula rather than by unbalanced capacity. Holding both pressure formulas constant - no modelled contention whatsoever - still returns PASS, on a throughput delta of -0.035 and an escape delta of 0.0013, because the accept rule is a pure sign test with no magnitude floor. An acceptance criterion that fires at 0.0013 cannot separate the reported result from noise. Both committed tests are vacuous in the same direction: one asserts that the injected formulas are monotone, which tests the assumption, and the other asserts the sign of two values from run(), which a constant satisfies, so a stub with no simulation passes the suite. I record NOT_YET rather than FAIL for a specific reason: unlike its sibling unit 050, the hypothesis here survives assumption-stripping. HC-E shows that with zero injected pressure, accepted good output per attempt falls monotonically from 1.000 to 0.120 while the acceptance backlog grows to 5634, driven purely by the fixed acceptance capacity - which is exactly the mechanism the frozen hypothesis names. The finding is real and the producer's own model already contains it; the unit measured it with a metric capped at the acceptance capacity, which is why the injected formula had to do the work.
disposition_reason: This is the narrowest call in my twenty units and I want the reasoning visible rather than buried. The case for acceptance is strong: the frozen deliverable is fully met, which I cannot say of most units here - five concurrency levels genuinely swept against fixed acceptance capacity with both required metrics reported per level and 1000 per-slot records behind them. The 161496-byte measurement artifact regenerates byte for byte. The internal accounting is exact at every level, including a recovery loop that mutates and re-queues items without double-counting anything, which I checked specifically because that is where such simulations usually break. The assumptions are published verbatim in the preregister and the limitation explicitly calls the contention formulas frozen and synthetic. Bytecode hygiene is deliberate and correct, and the one line responsible - sys.dont_write_bytecode - is exactly what its sibling unit 050 omitted. Nothing is invented. What tips it to rejection is that the preregistered accept rule returns PASS after I remove the mechanism it exists to detect, on an escape delta of 0.0013, because it is a sign test with no effect-size floor; and that both tests pass against a stub with no simulation in it. Those two together mean the unit's own instruments cannot tell its finding from noise, whatever the finding's merits. The remedy is narrow and I have already measured it for them: report accepted good per attempt rather than per slot, add a magnitude floor to the accept rule, read the compared levels from the preregister instead of hardcoding 4 and 32, and have one test assert an accounting identity. On the per-attempt metric the effect is 1.000 down to 0.120 with no injected pressure at all - a stronger and genuinely non-assumed result than the one reported.
